title: 5. Session Management
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L10: Web Security 1 (Injection · Auth · Access Control · Sessions): 5. Session Management.

items: HTTP is stateless — every request is independent
Session = server's mechanism to remember "this request belongs to user X"
Implementation: server-side store + opaque token in cookie

blocks.text: A session token is a bearer credential — anyone holding it IS the user, until it expires.

items: Unpredictable — never derived from user_id, timestamp, sequence
Server-side validatable — invalidation on logout must be effective immediately
Hijacking — XSS steals cookie via document.cookie; network sniff (no TLS)
Fixation — attacker forces a known session ID, victim authenticates with it
Replay — old token still valid because server didn't invalidate on logout
HttpOnly — JavaScript cannot read via document.cookie
SameSite=Strict (or Lax) — blocks cross-site cookie attachment
__Host- prefix — browser enforces Secure + Path=/ + no Domain attribute

blocks.text: ``python app.config.update( SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Strict', PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME=1800, # 30-min idle timeout ) ``

``python def login(username, password): user = verify(username, password) if user: session.clear() session.regenerate() # ← prevents fixation session['user_id'] = user.id session['created_at'] = time.time() ``
